Returns the median sale price, a typical range (10th–90th percentile), the number of sales, the period covered, a confidence label, and the official source and licence, from government sale records. Do not use for rents, asking prices, commercial property, or other countries.

country.description: AT = Austria (official STATISTIK AUSTRIA median price per m² of houses and flats, annual); AU = Australia (the Australian Bureau of Statistics' official mean price of residential dwellings, by state and territory; an official statistic of the whole dwelling stock, not individual sales and not a suburb price); BE = Belgium (official Statbel median sale prices by property type, quarterly); DK = Denmark (official average price per property from Statistics Denmark, by province and region; an official statistic, not individual sales); Eurostat house price index (2015 = 100, an official index, NOT a price in money) for: BG = Bulgaria, HR = Croatia, CY = Cyprus, CZ = Czechia, DE = Germany, EE = Estonia, ES = Spain, HU = Hungary, IS = Iceland, IT = Italy, LV = Latvia, LT = Lithuania, LU = Luxembourg, MT = Malta, PL = Poland, RO = Romania, SK = Slovakia, SI = Slovenia; FI = Finland (official average price per m² of old dwellings in housing companies from Statistics Finland, by municipality, region or postcode; an official statistic, not individual sales); FR = France (DVF); GB = England & Wales (HM Land Registry); IE = Ireland (Property Price Register); NL = Netherlands (official CBS average sale price per municipality, annual); NO = Norway (official average price per m² from Statistics Norway, by municipality or county; an official statistic, not individual sales); PT = Portugal (official INE median sale price per m², quarterly, by region and municipality); SE = Sweden (official average purchase price from Statistics Sweden, by municipality or county; an official statistic, not individual sales); SG = Singapore HDB resale flats; TW = Taiwan (Ministry of the Interior actual price registration: every registered sale, summarised by city or county and district); US = United States, partial: Connecticut, New York City and Cook County IL (Chicago area) only; not nationwide

county.description: IE only: same as town; a county such as 'Dublin' or 'Cork'.

months.description: How many recent months to include. Default 12. AT: ignored; STATISTIK AUSTRIA publishes one figure per calendar year (the latest is returned). AU: not used; the ABS publishes one mean price per quarter. BE: ignored; Statbel publishes quarters, half-years and years, and the latest period with a figure for the place is returned. DK: not used; Statistics Denmark publishes one average per quarter. BG HR CY CZ DE EE ES HU IS IT LV LT LU MT PL RO SI SK: ignored; the newest quarter with a figure is returned, with the change over the previous quarter and over a year. FI: not used; Statistics Finland publishes one average per quarter (postcodes, cities) or year (municipalities). IE: rounded to the nearest of 3, 6, 12, 24 or 36. NL: ignored; CBS publishes one average per calendar year (the latest is returned). NO: not used; Statistics Norway publishes one figure per quarter and the answer gives the latest quarter plus the previous one and a year earlier. PT: ignored; INE publishes one median per quarter, covering the 12 months to the quarter's end (the latest is returned). SE: not used; Statistics Sweden publishes one figure per year (municipalities, flats) or quarter (counties). TW: 12 or 24 whole calendar months; up to 18 gives 12 (24 if a place has too few sales in 12), more gives 24. The window ends at the last month that is at least 30 days old. US: 1 to 36 months back from the latest sale in the file (New York City: up to 12).

postcode.description: Postcode, for a precise area. AT: only Vienna postcodes (1010 to 1230) are matched, to the Vienna district; elsewhere give the town or district as town. AU: a 4-digit postcode ('2150'), answered with the state or territory it lies in (the ABS has no postcode figures). BE: not supported (Statbel publishes by municipality); give the municipality as town. DK: not supported (Statistics Denmark publishes by province and region); give town instead. BG HR CY CZ DE EE ES HU IS IT LV LT LU MT PL RO SI SK: not supported (national index only). FI: a five-digit postcode (for example 00100): the latest quarterly figure for that postal code area. Flats are published by number of rooms, so the answer is the room size with most transactions and the others are listed. FR: 5-digit postcode, e.g. '69003'; use instead of town for a precise area. NL: not supported (CBS publishes by municipality); give the municipality as town. NO: not supported (Statistics Norway publishes by municipality); give town instead. PT: not supported (INE publishes by region and municipality); give the municipality as town. SE: not supported (Statistics Sweden publishes by municipality); give town instead. TW: not supported (the register has no postcodes); give the city, county or district as town. US: 5-digit ZIP code, New York City only (Connecticut and Cook County have no ZIP in the public file).

postcode_district.description: GB only: postcode district such as 'BS8' to narrow the area.

property_type.description: Kind of home. Default 'any'. AT: house or apartment (flats). The figure is the price per m² of living area. With no type given the headline is the flat figure and both medians are in extra.by_type. There is no figure for both together or for villas, detached, semi-detached or terraced homes. AU: not split by the ABS; the figure covers all residential dwellings (houses and attached dwellings together). Any value is accepted and noted. BE: house (all houses, not apartments), apartment, or detached / villa (houses with 4 or more facades), semi-detached or terraced (houses with 2 or 3 facades). Statbel has no figure for houses and apartments together, so without a type you get both medians in the summary and no single price. DK: house (one-family houses), flat (owner-occupied flats). Without a type, the group with more sales in that place is answered and the other is in extra. Detached and terraced are not published separately. BG HR CY CZ DE EE ES HU IS IT LV LT LU MT PL RO SI SK: ignored; the index covers all dwellings (new and existing) bought by households. FI: flat (flats in blocks of flats), terraced (terraced houses, which also include detached houses with shares in a housing company). Without a type, all building types. House and detached are not covered. FR: house or apartment. GB: detached, semi-detached, terraced or flat-maisonette. IE: any, new or second-hand (new homes are usually recorded without VAT). NL: CBS does not split this figure by home type; only 'any' (all existing owner-occupied homes) has an answer. NO: any (all dwellings, default), house or detached (detached houses), terraced (row houses), flat (multi-dwelling buildings). Official price per m² of existing dwellings. PT: INE splits by number of bedrooms, not by house or apartment; only 'any' has an answer (the answer includes the split by bedrooms). SE: house (one- and two-dwelling buildings; the default for any), flat (tenant-owned flats, median price, county or metropolitan area only). Villas, terraced and semi-detached houses are not split, so detached and terraced return no figure. TW: apartment (high-rise, mid-rise and walk-up flats together), house (透天厝), high-rise (住宅大樓, 11+ floors with a lift), mid-rise (華廈, up to 10 floors with a lift) or walk-up (公寓, up to 5 floors, no lift). Default any = all homes. US: any (default), house (one- to three-family houses and townhomes), condo, or coop (New York City only).

state.description: US only: 'CT' (Connecticut), 'NY' (New York City) or 'IL' (Cook County). Usually inferred from the place; set it when a name exists in two of them.

town.description: Town or city. AT: a municipality among the 100 largest ('Wien' / 'Vienna', 'Graz', 'Linz', 'Salzburg', 'Innsbruck'), a district ('Wien 2' for Leopoldstadt, 'Bezirk Baden', 'Kitzbühel'), or a Bundesland ('Tirol', 'Niederösterreich' / 'Lower Austria'). Omit for Austria. Official annual medians per m², not a list of sales. AU: a state or territory ('Victoria', 'NSW', 'Queensland', 'Tasmania', 'ACT'), or a city or town that lies in one ('Melbourne', 'Parramatta', 'Perth'). The ABS publishes by state and territory only, so a city is answered with its state (and the answer says so). Omit for Australia as a whole. BE: a municipality in Dutch, French or English ('Antwerpen' / 'Antwerp' / 'Anvers', 'Gent' / 'Ghent', 'Brussel' / 'Bruxelles' / 'Brussels', 'Liège'), or a province ('province of Namur') or region ('Flanders', 'Wallonia', 'Brussels Capital Region'). Omit for Belgium. Official Statbel medians, not a list of sales. DK: a municipality or town ('København' or 'Copenhagen', 'Aarhus' or 'Århus', 'Odense', 'Aalborg'), a province ('Fyn', 'Østjylland', 'Nordsjælland') or a region ('Hovedstaden', 'Syddanmark'), with or without æ ø å. Statistics Denmark publishes by province, so a municipality is answered with the province it lies in (and the answer says which). Omit for Denmark as a whole. BG HR CY CZ DE EE ES HU IS IT LV LT LU MT PL RO SI SK: ignored; Eurostat publishes one national index per country. The answer is an index (2015 = 100), not a price in euros. FI: a municipality ('Helsinki' or 'Helsingfors', 'Espoo', 'Tampere', 'Oulu', 'Hämeenlinna'), a region ('Uusimaa', 'Pirkanmaa'), 'Greater Helsinki', with or without ä ö å. Omit for Finland as a whole. Larger cities, regions and the country have quarterly figures (with the official price-index changes); other municipalities have the latest yearly figure. FR: town, e.g. 'Bordeaux', or use postcode. GB: required, e.g. 'Bristol'. IE: a county ('Cork') or Dublin postal district ('Dublin 6'). Omit for all of Ireland. NL: a municipality ('Amsterdam', 'Den Haag' / 'The Hague' / 's-Gravenhage, 'Utrecht') or a province ('Noord-Holland'). Omit for the national average. Official CBS annual average, not a list of sales. NO: a municipality ('Oslo', 'Bergen', 'Tromsø' or 'Tromso', 'Stavanger') or a county ('Rogaland', 'Vestland'), Norwegian or Sami spelling, with or without æ ø å. Omit for the whole country. Answers are Statistics Norway's published average price per m² (NOK) with the number of sales, not a list of sales. PT: a municipality INE publishes ('Lisboa' / 'Lisbon', 'Porto' / 'Oporto', 'Cascais', 'Faro', 'Funchal' ... 58 in all) or a region ('Algarve', 'Grande Lisboa', 'Madeira', 'Açores'). Omit for Portugal as a whole. Official INE median per m² of the last 12 months of sales, not a list of sales. SE: a municipality ('Stockholm', 'Göteborg' or 'Gothenburg', 'Malmö' or 'Malmo', 'Uppsala'), a county ('Skåne', 'Stockholms län') or a metropolitan area ('Greater Gothenburg'), with or without å ä ö. Omit for Sweden as a whole. Answers are Statistics Sweden's published average purchase price (SEK per home) with the number of sales, not a list of sales. SG: required, one of the 26 HDB towns, e.g. 'Tampines', 'Ang Mo Kio', 'Bukit Merah', 'Kallang/Whampoa', 'Central Area' (case, hyphens and ', Singapore' are forgiven; 'Kallang' and 'CBD' are understood). TW: a city or county in English or Chinese ('Taipei' / '台北市' / '臺北市', 'New Taipei', 'Taichung', 'Kaohsiung', 'Tainan', 'Taoyuan', 'Hsinchu City', 'Hsinchu County'), or a district with its city ("Da'an, Taipei", '臺北市大安區', 'Banqiao, New Taipei'). Omit for all of Taiwan. A district name used in several cities ('Zhongzheng', 'Dongqu') needs the city too. US: a Connecticut town ('Hartford'), a New York City borough or neighborhood ('Brooklyn', 'Williamsburg'), 'Chicago', 'Cook County' or a Cook County assessment township ('Evanston', 'Oak Park'). Add the state if a name exists in two places ('Hartford, CT'). Required unless postcode is a New York City ZIP.

name: pricepaid_home_sales

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.
